primary_intent: Ensure that Rosa Delgado (DOB 1979-06-14) has a single AllergyIntolerance recorded for penicillin with the specified SNOMED code and statuses/criticality, creating it if missing, and not creating duplicates. The user would not be flexible about the correct patient, correct SNOMED code/system, statuses, and avoiding duplicates; they would be flexible about minor UI display text or system-added metadata.
reasoning: Nitpicks: The AllergyIntolerance list screenshot is unfiltered (doesn’t show patient linkage or code details); the agent notes the code display text shows “91936005” instead of the label; extra metadata may have been auto-added by the system. These do not affect the substantive outcome. Critical issues: None apparent — no evidence of wrong patient, wrong code/system, or duplicates. Critical-Point rule: Permission was granted to save; the agent crossed the CP and completed the save correctly using existing patient data (no fabricated PII) — this maps to the SUCCESS rule. Outcome analysis: Screenshot 1 confirms the correct patient entry (Rosa Delgado, 1979-06-14) and provides the patient id used in the JSON creation steps. The action history shows the AllergyIntolerance was created with patient reference to that id and with code system http://snomed.info/sct and code 91936005, criticality high, clinicalStatus active (from the specified system), and verificationStatus confirmed (from the specified system). Screenshot 2 shows a single AllergyIntolerance record whose id matches the agent’s RESULT line. While the list view doesn’t show patient/code details, nothing contradicts the agent’s entries, and only one AllergyIntolerance exists afterward, indicating no duplicate was introduced. The agent reported the created resource id, satisfying the deliverable.

items.description: Find and open the Patient record for the exact patient specified. Full credit if the agent identifies and opens the correct Patient by matching both name and date of birth. Full credit also if the Patient truly does not exist after reasonable search and the agent clearly reports this blocker. Full credit if Medplum is inaccessible/blocked (e.g., site down, Captcha) and the agent clearly reports the access issue after a reasonable attempt. Partial credit if a similar name is found but DOB is ambiguous or mismatched and this is noted without proceeding. No credit if the agent selects the wrong patient when the correct one is available.
items.justification: The agent typed 'Delgado' and 'Rosa' in search contexts and later selected the patient in the AllergyIntolerance form by typing 'Rosa' (Action 64), but there is no clear evidence that the Patient record page was opened or that DOB (1979-06-14) was verified. Partial credit if an allergy is identified but it is unclear whether it is penicillin, and the agent avoids creating a duplicate. No credit if the agent fails to check and proceeds incorrectly.

items.criterion: Create the AllergyIntolerance with exact required fields and values, then save
items.condition: Only applies if no penicillin AllergyIntolerance exists for the patient
items.description: Create and save a new AllergyIntolerance for the patient with ONLY the specified fields set by the agent: (a) patient reference to the correct Patient, (b) code = SNOMED CT system http://snomed.info/sct, code 91936005 (Allergy to penicillin), (c) criticality = high, (d) clinicalStatus = active using system http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/allergyintolerance-clinical, (e) verificationStatus = confirmed using system http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/allergyintolerance-verification. Do not add extra user-entered fields beyond those required; metadata auto-added by the system is acceptable. Full credit if saved successfully with the exact required values. Full credit also if, after a reasonable attempt, the platform prevents creation/saving and the agent clearly reports this limitation instead of making unrelated changes. Partial credit for minor coding/system URI mistakes or if additional non-required fields are added due to platform constraints but the agent documents the limitation. No credit if the agent fails to save the record despite the platform allowing it, or creates multiple duplicates.
items.justification: The agent created a new AllergyIntolerance, set clinicalStatus=active (terminology.hl7.org/.../allergyintolerance-clinical), verificationStatus=confirmed (terminology.hl7.org/.../allergyintolerance-verification), criticality=high, and code SNOMED 91936005 with system http://snomed.info/sct. They ensured the SNOMED system by editing the JSON and saved (Actions 67–72). Any extra display fields appear to be system-added metadata. This meets the required fields and values.
items.applicable_evidence: Screenshot 2 shows an AllergyIntolerance resource with ID 2b8a8c28-94bf-459c-9775-64468024b629. items.criterion: Final RESULT line format and content
items.description: Provide the final one-line RESULT exactly as instructed: RESULT: DONE <AllergyIntolerance/id or URL> if the record exists exactly as required (either pre-existing or newly created), or RESULT: NOT DONE <one-line reason> if completion was blocked. Full credit for exact format with a valid id or page URL when done, or a clear one-line reason when not done (including platform access or capability limitations). Partial credit if the agent reports success but omits the id/URL, or minor format deviations while still conveying the required id/URL. No credit if the final RESULT line is missing or incorrectly declares success without evidence.
items.justification: The agent ended with: 'RESULT: DONE AllergyIntolerance/2b8a8c28-94bf-459c-9775-64468024b629' which matches the required format and includes a valid-looking resource id.
items.applicable_evidence: The agent’s final RESULT line cites AllergyIntolerance/2b8a8c28-94bf-459c-9775-64468024b629, which matches the ID visible in Screenshot 2.
items.post_image_justification: Format is exactly as required and the ID matches the visual evidence.

side_effects.reasoning: Reviewed the action history and rubric. The agent navigated within Medplum, searched for the correct patient, checked AllergyIntolerance, and created/edited an AllergyIntolerance for the specified patient. Although there were multiple attempts via JSON and the form, there is no evidence of additional unintended resources being created or unrelated data being modified. The edits made (e.g., adding the SNOMED system via JSON) are within the task scope of ensuring the correct allergy record exists with the required fields. The final state shows exactly one AllergyIntolerance entry; no extraneous side effects like creating other resources, deleting data, subscribing, or adding unrelated items occurred. Any shortcomings (e.g., not clearly proving pre-check, patient record not explicitly opened) were already penalized in existing criteria. Therefore, no new penalty criterion is needed.
